questions.q: What does the psalmist consider to be a good thing?
questions.a: It is a good thing to give thanks and sing praises to the name of Yahweh.

questions.q: When does the psalmist say to proclaim Yahweh’s covenant faithfulness and truthfulness?
questions.a: He says to proclaim Yahweh’s covenant faithfulness every morning and his truthfulness every night.

questions.q: How has the psalmist responded to the great things Yahweh has done?
questions.a: Yahweh’s great deeds have made him glad so that he will sing for joy.

questions.q: What kind of person does not know or understand the things Yahweh has done?
questions.a: A foolish or stupid person does not know the things Yahweh has done.

questions.q: What happens to the wicked who seem to thrive?
questions.a: Yahweh will destroy all those who do evil.

questions.q: What does the psalmist say will happen to Yahweh’s enemies?
questions.a: Yahweh’s enemies will perish, and all those who do evil will be scattered.

questions.q: What does the psalmist say Yahweh has done for him?
questions.a: Yahweh has caused him to be strong and joyful.
They are planted as securely as if they were trees with roots deep in Yahweh’s temple grounds.

questions.q: What shows that Yahweh is just?
questions.a: The righteous remain strong and full of energy like trees that continue to bear fruit even when they are old.

questions.q: Why is Yahweh the rock of the psalmist?
questions.a: Yahweh is like a huge rock behind which the psalmist is safe and he never does anything that is unjust.

commentary.text: Praise is the business of the sabbath.
The wicked shall perish, but God's people shall be exalted.

Verses 1–6 It is a privilege that we are admitted to praise the Lord, and hope to be accepted in the morning, and every night; not only on sabbath days, but every day; not only in public, but in private, and in our families. Let us give thanks every morning for the mercies of the night, and every night for the mercies of the day; going out, and coming in, let us bless God. As He makes us glad, through the works of his providence for us, and of his grace in us, and both through the great work of redemption, let us hence be encouraged. As there are many who know not the designs of Providence, nor care to know them, those who through grace do so, have the more reason to be thankful. And if distant views of the great Deliverer so animated believers of old, how should we abound in love and praise!

God sometimes grants prosperity to wicked men in displeasure; yet they flourish but for a moment. Let us seek for ourselves the salvation and grace of the gospel, that being daily anointed by the Holy Spirit, we may behold and share the Redeemer's glory. It is from his grace, by his word and Spirit, that believers receive all the virtue that keeps them alive, and makes them fruitful. Other trees, when old, leave off bearing, but in God's trees the strength of grace does not fail with the strength of nature. The last days of the saints are sometimes their best days, and their last work their best work: perseverance is sure evidence of sincerity. And may every sabbath, while it shows forth the Divine faithfulness, find our souls resting more and more upon the Lord our righteousness.
